scenes.title: Porcelain rat pressing a brass lever hundreds of times an hour beneath a flexible overhead lead
scenes.era: 1954, McGill University psychology basement laboratory, Montreal

layout.description: High-key 1954 Montreal neuroscience laboratory featuring a clear-fronted wooden Skinner lever box with a counterweighted flexible overhead wire commutator connected to a 60-hertz variable transformer and a steep cumulative paper-drum recorder.

positions.where: rearing eagerly at the front wall of the chamber pressing the wide brass lever repeatedly with both forepaws

positions.who: James Olds (mannequin in 1950s white lab coat and rolled sleeves)
positions.where: leaning beside the cumulative recorder drum holding a stopwatch
positions.facing: staring at the nearly vertical ink line

positions.who: Peter Milner (mannequin in tweed vest and white lab coat)
positions.where: adjusting the 60-hertz transformer dial on the wooden bench

props.name: wide brass self-stimulation lever
props.period_detail: polished horizontal brass pedal mounted inside the chamber wall
props.physical_behavior: depresses rhythmically multiple times every ten seconds while a full food dish behind the rat sits untouched

props.name: overhead counterweighted wire arm
props.period_detail: balanced 1950s pivot arm allowing free movement inside the box
props.physical_behavior: sways gently with each rapid lever press

props.name: steep cumulative ink-drum graph
props.period_detail: rotating white paper cylinder where the ink pen climbs at a near-vertical 1,920-per-hour angle

actions.verb_sequence: turns completely away from a full ceramic food dish -> rushes to the brass pedal -> presses rapidly again and again
flip the current toggle OFF for thirty seconds watching pressing halt -> flip it ON and watch the rat lunge straight back to the pedal

reactions.reaction: maintains intense forward-leaning seeking posture over the brass lever
points to the untouched food dish beside the near-vertical ink trace in astonishment

scenes.wardrobe: 1954 McGill researchers in white cotton lab coats over collared shirts and ties; subject staged as an articulated matte-white porcelain rat sculpture.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key 1950s laboratory daylight across wooden benches, brass lever, and white paper drum.
scenes.recognition_hook: Ignoring a full dish of food right behind it, an articulated porcelain rat presses a brain-wired brass lever nearly two thousand times an hour.

key_visual.description: an articulated porcelain rat pressing a brass lever relentlessly inside a clear McGill chamber while ignoring a full food dish beside a near-vertical paper-drum graph

scenes.title: Rat #34 returning to the open tabletop corner instead of fleeing

layout.description: Large open wooden tabletop arena surrounded by low walls where James Olds holds a manual push-button switch.

positions.where: trotting eagerly back into the marked northeast corner of the arena sniffing the air
standing tableside thumbing a handheld bakelite push-button

props.name: handheld bakelite stimulation button
props.physical_behavior: each click draws the porcelain rat straight back to the corner

actions.verb_sequence: clicks the handheld switch -> Rat #34 pivots and marches straight back to that exact corner

reactions.reaction: realizes his electrode missed the aversive midbrain target and hit an unknown reward zone

scenes.wardrobe: 1950s white lab coat; porcelain rat sculpture.
scenes.recognition_hook: Instead of running away from the pulse, Rat #34 marched straight back for more.

scenes.title: X-ray reveal of the bent electrode wire

layout.description: Clean backlit X-ray viewer showing a crisp cranial radiograph where the thin wire curves anteriorly into the septal forebrain region.

positions.where: standing side-by-side pointing a pencil tip at the forward bend on the backlit X-ray plate

props.name: backlit X-ray plate
props.period_detail: monochrome cranial radiograph showing the bent electrode trajectory
props.physical_behavior: reveals septal / medial forebrain placement several millimeters ahead of target

actions.verb_sequence: traces the bent wire arc on the lightbox from midbrain target to anterior septum

reactions.reaction: smiles as the surgical mistake explains the behavioral reversal

scenes.lighting: Crisp lightbox illumination in bright room.
scenes.recognition_hook: A backlit X-ray revealed the bent silver wire had landed squarely in the forebrain reward highway.

scenes.title: Catching late-night 'wanting without liking' on a smartphone

layout.description: Clean modern desk where a person mannequin pauses mid-thumb-scroll, notices their own blank expression, and sets the phone onto a charging dock across the room.

positions.where: sitting at desk pausing thumb above glowing feed, then placing phone on far shelf

props.name: smartphone and distant wooden dock
props.physical_behavior: placed out of arm's reach to break the subcortical lever loop

actions.verb_sequence: catches automatic thumb-flick -> pauses -> walks phone across room onto wooden stand

reactions.reaction: shoulders drop with calm relief once the lever is out of reach

scenes.recognition_hook: Asking 'am I actually enjoying this, or just pressing the lever?' breaks the wanting trance.
